currentUse: The former St. Joseph Roman Catholic church at 301 South State Street stands in Orthodox use. St. Nicholas Orthodox Church reports purchasing it in April 2020 and adapting it as its present church. St. Joseph is not listed as a current separate parish in the Diocese of Erie directory.
summary: St. Joseph was DuBois's Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish and is directly documented as active by 1912. It must be kept separate from a less-defined Lithuanian independent or national Catholic effort reported in DuBois in 1903; the surviving evidence does not establish that the two were the same institution. St. Joseph's church at 301 South State Street survived after the parish ceased operating independently. St. Nicholas Orthodox Church reports purchasing the former Roman Catholic church in April 2020 and converting it for Orthodox worship, while the Diocese of Erie's current directory serves DuBois through Holy Spirit Parish and no longer lists St. Joseph as a separate parish. The exact establishment date, suppression or merger act, date of the last Mass, destination of parish and sacramental records, and relationship to Holy Spirit Parish remain unresolved. The standing building's Orthodox use is established by its current congregation, but civil deed confirmation and a complete institutional chronology are still needed.

historicalNarrative.text: Lithuanian Catholics established a Roman Catholic parish life in DuBois by the early twentieth century. A contemporary 1912 Draugas notice names St. Joseph Parish in DuBois and records parish fundraising and accounting activity, providing direct evidence of an organized Catholic institution rather than only a later heritage memory. The exact founding date has not yet been recovered from an official parish or diocesan history.

historicalNarrative.text: The St. Joseph record is Roman Catholic. A separate 1984 history says an independent or national Lithuanian church appeared in DuBois in 1903, but it does not name that effort St. Joseph or tie it to the later parish. Until a contemporary charter, clergy notice, or property record establishes a connection, the 1903 national effort cannot be used as St. Joseph's founding date or denomination.

historicalNarrative.text: The parish's material legacy included the St. Joseph church at 301 South State Street, a Lithuanian cemetery, and a broader network of community institutions remembered in later heritage reporting. By 2018 the church and cemetery were being documented as surviving Lithuanian places in DuBois, although the parish was no longer visible as a current standalone institution in the diocesan structure.

sources.locator: Draugas, 2018-01-11, p. 4: DuBois Lithuanian church, cemetery, and community heritage

historicalNarrative.text: The church building entered a new religious life in 2020. St. Nicholas Orthodox Church states that it purchased the former St. Joseph Roman Catholic Church in April of that year and adapted the property for Orthodox worship. The Diocese of Erie's current directory lists Holy Spirit Parish as DuBois's Roman Catholic parish and does not list St. Joseph separately, confirming the end of independent St. Joseph operations without supplying the missing canonical decree or records-transfer history.

historicalNarrative.text: Several institutional questions remain unanswered even though the building outcome is clear. No official source reviewed here gives St. Joseph's exact founding, suppression, or merger date; identifies the last pastor or final Mass; or states where sacramental and corporate records went. The Orthodox congregation's account establishes present use, while county deeds and diocesan archives are still needed to complete the legal and canonical sequence.

developments.headline: Contemporary report documents St. Joseph Parish
developments.detail: A Draugas parish-accounting item names St. Joseph Parish in DuBois and documents active fundraising. This is the earliest directly reviewed evidence presently attached to the Roman Catholic parish.

developments.headline: Former St. Joseph church purchased for Orthodox use
developments.detail: St. Nicholas Orthodox Church reports purchasing the former St. Joseph Roman Catholic Church at 301 South State Street in April 2020 and adapting it as its worship home. The structure remains standing in religious use.

developments.headline: Current Catholic directory no longer lists St. Joseph separately
developments.detail: The Diocese of Erie directory lists Holy Spirit Parish for DuBois and no separate St. Joseph parish. The exact canonical end and records destination remain unresolved.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The canonical row is the Roman Catholic St. Joseph parish, directly attested in 1912 and identified as Roman Catholic by the present Orthodox user of its former building. The 1903 DuBois independent or national Catholic effort is a separate, under-specified record and must not supply St. Joseph's class or founding date without a linking source. The former St. Joseph church stands in Orthodox use; the precise canonical end of the parish is still not established.
gaps: No official parish foundation history, suppression or merger decree, last-Mass date, records-transfer notice, complete clergy list, or civil deed has been found. The title and physical history of the separate 1903 national Catholic effort remain unresolved. Diocesan archives and Clearfield County property records are needed to complete both institutional lines.
